decision: Provider intelligence must be conditional and multidimensional: direction, session/time, weekday, observable regime/volatility/liquidity, TP progression, management quality, duplicates, latency/slippage, provider agreement/conflict, geometry, adverse duration and recovery behaviour. Deterministic duplicate rejection and obvious exposure conflicts should be evaluated first; provider/regime denies and early-close management follow only with prospective evidence, kill switches and explicit owner/live gates.
reason: Prevent duplicate losing or conflicting positions while making AIDY useful quickly without silently changing the existing 1% risk contract.

decision: A single startup-probe log line ("AIDY Provider Context live probe READY") is architecturally incapable of proving sustained health -- it fires once per process lifetime and never repeats. Verifying continued health requires checking AIDY's own D1 market_snapshots for a run of consecutive complete rows and Super Signals' own resolver-progress tables (aidy_m1_cursor_at advancing), not one probe line. This session verified 53/53 complete snapshots and 83 actively-updated shadow_trades rows across multiple cycles before treating AIDY as healthy.

When a background job fails with a caught exception, log str(exc) alongside the exception type, never the type alone -- PROVIDER_DAY14_GOVERNANCE_ERROR=RuntimeError cost a full database forensics session to diagnose when the actual guard name was in the message the whole time. Applied as a general fix pattern, same as the AIDY research_fetch_failed lesson from 2026-09-15.

Owner gave a standing mandate: profit is the explicit goal (growing the balance or preventing losses, same goal), AIDY must become a full evidence-scored decision layer that knows each signal group's behaviour, can approve/deny/close-early/hold signals with explained reasoning, and must be continuously measurable on whether its decisions actually helped. Owner authorizes Claude to make routine engineering and product decisions without asking first, to propose costed spend up to roughly EUR200/month beyond existing ~EUR500/month costs, and to build new infrastructure (dashboards, databases, services) as needed. Full text pinned at OWNER_MANDATE.md so it does not need repeating. The one boundary this does not touch: AIDY's live-money/broker execution authority stays OFF and the 1% live-risk directive does not change silently -- both already stood as AGENTS.md rules before this mandate and remain in force, restated explicitly so 'full access to everything' is never later misread as having quietly overridden them.

Owner directive: paper (demo-account) and real-money execution must run through exactly one pipeline, always, treated with equal seriousness -- never forked by account mode or balance size. Risk scales proportionally (the selected risk percent of whatever the actual funded balance is, EUR50 or EUR10,000) rather than by tier. Verified 2026-09-17 that the architecture already satisfies this: active_account_execution.py's _load_demo_account is a direct alias of _load_active_account, risk_sizing_day24.py computes purely from the real broker balance with an explicit small-account overexposure guard, and 4 currently-testing (paper) sources run through the identical positions table and execution path as live sources. Recorded as a standing constraint on all future work, including the AIDY decision layer: never add an is_paper or balance-threshold branch to execution or sizing logic. Found and fixed a real pre-existing test-infra bug while building the Decision Ledger: services/api/migrations/env.py unconditionally called logging.config.fileConfig() on every Alembic migration, which replaces the root logger's handlers process-wide and silently discards pytest's caplog capture handler for the rest of that test session, not just the test that ran the migration. It had never been triggered before because no alembic-invoking test file happened to sort alphabetically before test_aidy_shadow_runtime_startup.py; the new test_aidy_decision_ledger.py was the first. Fixed by skipping fileConfig() when PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST is set in the environment; real CLI/deploy usage is unaffected. General lesson: a test file's fixture side effects on global process state (logging config, env vars, monkeypatches left unreverted) can silently break unrelated tests purely by alphabetical file-collection order -- worth checking full-suite runs, not just the new file in isolation, before trusting a build is regression-free.

Built and shipped AIDY decision outcome scoring (PR #184): every decision now scores against provider_trade_scores as a fixed baseline, reused rather than re-derived since AIDY holds no live authority yet so the real trade already is the provider's unmodified plan. approve/continue always equals the baseline (delta=0, never manufactured credit); deny/conflict_deny/hold is scored as if the trade was never taken, so a denied trade that really lost reads confirmed_helped and one that really won reads confirmed_hurt, purely from the sign of an already-computed number. aidy_decision_outcomes is write-once by construction (append-only, unique per decision) -- a trade still open_at_window_end is scored with interim mark-to-market figures but flagged with that same resolution since it is the only row that decision will ever get.
